what_it_does: checks workstream ids, parent links and cycles, then requires gcLiaison and tcSponsor roles and checks each sponsor against three membership sets built from people.yml, rebuilding those sets for every workstream

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: gc_members, tc_members and spec_sponsors are set comprehensions over people_data, which the loop never changes, yet they are rebuilt for every workstream. Hoisting them above the loop builds each set once. Nothing mutates them: spec_sponsors is a new set from the union, and the checks only test membership. This matches the card's first repair, a set rebuilt on every iteration.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: parent_kind is assigned from a dict lookup and a get, and nothing reads it. The lookup cannot raise, because line 99 has already continued on a missing parent. Deleting the line removes one lookup per workstream that has a parent and changes no output.

what_it_does: fetches one GitHub user record by login over HTTPS and returns its canonical login, or None when the status is not 200

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: requests.get at 137 opens a new connection for every login, so each lookup pays TCP and TLS setup before its request. Keeping one requests.Session on the function, created on the first call, reuses the connection across the loop. URL, headers, status handling and return value stay the same. The card's bulk form would be a GraphQL batch, which changes the function's contract, so this is the closest per-request fix and the attribution is close. Blocked here, because it needs the GitHub API.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The lookups are independent waits, which is the shape C11.S5 describes. Overlapping them changes the contract. The sleep at 130 and the request rate exist to stay under GitHub's rate limit, and the 'Getting GitHub login for' and 'Failed to retrieve' prints would come out in completion order rather than input order. The waits are idle time, so the energy case is weak as well. Rejected on the printed-output and rate-limit checks.

what_it_does: walks the devstats frames, looks up each login through get_github_login, and collects [login, contributions] rows for the logins that resolve

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: zip(names, contributions) would replace the index loop, but it is not equivalent. If contributions is shorter than names, the original raises IndexError, and zip stops quietly. zip with strict=True raises ValueError, a different exception type. The index work is two subscripts per row against one HTTP request per row inside get_github_login, so the saving would be negligible even where it applies. Rejected on the exception-type check.

what_it_does: gathers the bare-metal jobs from every completed run of each listed workflow and returns one record per job with its duration, queue wait and run identity

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: parse_iso(started) is evaluated at 114 for the duration, at 124 for the queue wait, and at 134 for the record. One parse bound to a local serves all three. The parse at 114 already sits inside the try that catches ValueError, so a bad timestamp still skips the job, and the later uses cannot see a bad string. Two fromisoformat calls are removed per job. Blocked here, because the function runs the gh CLI against GitHub.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: parse_iso(run_started_at) at 124 runs for every job, but run_started_at is set once per run at line 90. Parsing it once per run, inside a try that falls back to None, keeps the queue wait at 0.0 on a bad run timestamp, exactly as the per-job try does. This removes one parse per job after the first job of each run. Blocked here, for the same reason as a.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: One gh api call per run is the only way this data is listed. The jobs endpoint takes one run id, and no bulk endpoint returns the jobs of many runs. The bulk repair would replace the gh subprocess with an HTTP client, which changes authentication and pagination, so no edit to this function keeps its contract. Rejected: no repair.

what_it_does: returns the markdown table rows for one group of SIGs, one row per workstream with a link to its details section

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: extract_row_data(ws) at 372 is recomputed for the same ws in render_sig_details. The value is the computed result of a deterministic function, which is what C8.S1 describes. C8.S2 covers compiled, parsed or prepared artefacts, so it is the wrong card. The duplicate is recorded again as c under C8.S1 and decided there.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: content is a plain local grown with += once per SIG row, at 374. CPython resizes an unaliased local string in place, so the quadratic copy the card describes may not happen here, and the card's measured form for a plain local is the join. The reading cannot settle it, so the measurement decides. A negligible or regressed result is likely.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: The same duplicate call as a, seen as a repeated deterministic computation across two call sites. The only in-unit repair is a memo on extract_row_data, which cannot be keyed safely (see the extract_row_data record). Rejected for that reason.

what_it_does: returns the detail section for one SIG: a heading and one bullet per non-empty field, with values taken from extract_row_data

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: extract_row_data(ws) at 381 repeats the call render_group made for the same ws. Same waste as render_group a, and the card is again C8.S1, not C8.S2. Decided under C8.S1 on extract_row_data.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The repeated computation of extract_row_data(ws) across two call sites. A memo would have to live on extract_row_data, and that cannot be keyed safely. Rejected for the same reason as the extract_row_data record.

what_it_does: turns one workstream dict into a dict of meeting, channel, repository, sponsor and liaison fields, each a list of link strings

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The function is deterministic in ws, and the same ws passes through it twice per run, so memoisation fits C8.S1 in form. The repair cannot be made safe. A memo keyed on id(ws) can return the rows of a different SIG once a dict is freed and its id reused, and a key on the ws content costs about as much as the function, so the cache saves nothing. No in-unit repair behaves identically on every input. Rejected on the behaviour check.

what_it_does: compares the @handles in existing voter comments with the roll, removes stale handles, and posts batches of voters that no comment mentions yet

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: extract_mentions runs on each voter comment body twice: at 332 to fill tagged_lower, and at 341 on the same original text for the removal pass. Computing the mention list once per comment, and reusing it in both loops, gives the same tagged set and the same removals, and removes one regex findall per comment. The bodies are short, so the saving is small. Measurable here with dryrun true, which makes no gh calls.

what_it_does: fetches a repo's issue comments since a cutoff, page by page, and returns a dict from each commenter to the PR and issue numbers they commented on, cached per repo

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The test number not in commenters[user][kind] at 256 searches a list for every comment, so a prolific commenter costs one linear search per comment. A seen-set per (user, kind), kept beside the lists, answers the same question in one hash probe. The lists keep their first-seen order, so the cached value is unchanged. This matches the card's second repair, a set beside a list that is still the answer. Blocked here, because the function fetches from the GitHub API.

what_it_does: filters the cached commenters of a repo to the requested users and comment kind, and returns each active user's list of numbers, minus an excluded PR

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The concatenation at 326 builds the list the function returns for a user who commented in either kind, and the caller prints that list in debug output in insertion order. Only the None path concatenates. The list has to exist to be returned, so the copy is the answer and not a spare copy, and no in-unit form returns the same value without building it. Rejected on the return-value check.

what_it_does: scans the cached repo events once and returns the first matching event of each user in remaining whose event type is in the requested set

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The loop at 343-349 scans every cached event even after every user in remaining already has an entry in found. found holds only members of remaining and keeps each actor's first event, so once len(found) equals len(remaining), no later event can change active, and a break at that point returns the same dict. The gain depends on the event list: it is large when candidates are found early, and small when they are found late or never, which is the usual case for inactive members. The function calls _get_repo_events, which fetches from GitHub unless its cache is warm, so the generator may fail on it.

what_it_does: for each candidate PR number, fetches the PR's reviews over REST, and returns the first PR on which the user reviewed on or after the cutoff

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The review list of a candidate PR is fetched again for every user who is a candidate on that PR, because the function keeps nothing between calls. A dict of review lists keyed by (repo, PR number), held for one run of the script, returns the same lists to each user. The lifetime is one run, which the function already assumes when it reads reviews as current. Blocked here, because it needs the GitHub API.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: One GraphQL query returning the reviews of all candidate PRs would replace the per-PR REST loop with one round trip. That rewrites the verification into a different query and response shape, so no edit to this function keeps its contract. Rejected: the repair is a rewrite, not an edit.

what_it_does: checks each batch of up to ten users for review activity with one GraphQL search, verifies candidate PRs over REST, and pages per user when the first page does not confirm

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: safe = u_ plus re.sub(...) is computed for each user in the alias loop at 433 and again in the result loop at 449, from the same user name. A dict of safe names built once per batch serves both loops. The saving is one re.sub per user per batch, which is microseconds beside the network calls. Blocked here, because the function sends GraphQL requests.

what_it_does: checks which triagers in a list were active on any of the repos since the cutoff, by comments, then label and close events, and returns the active set

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The debug call at 497 builds its message with _fmt_numbers(numbers), which joins every number of an active user, before debug() checks DEBUG and drops the text when DEBUG is off. Guarding that call with an if DEBUG test skips the join on every normal run, and prints the same text when DEBUG is on. Blocked here, because _check_comments fetches from GitHub.

what_it_does: checks which approvers were active since the cutoff through PR comments, issue comments and reviews, and returns the active set

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Three debug calls, at 541, 550 and 559, build their messages with _fmt_numbers before debug() discards them when DEBUG is off. Guarding these three calls with an if DEBUG test skips the joins, and the output with DEBUG on is unchanged. Blocked here, because the checks fetch from GitHub.

what_it_does: checks which maintainers were active since the cutoff through PR comments, issue comments, reviews, authored PRs and merges, and returns the active set

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Debug calls at 597, 606, 615 and 650 build their messages eagerly. Line 650 also runs _extract_numbers and _fmt_numbers on the authored-PR search result for every user with authored PRs. Guarding the four calls with an if DEBUG test skips that work when DEBUG is off. Blocked here, because the checks fetch from GitHub.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: _search_fields() at 633 sits inside the per-user loop at 630-636, but it returns a string fixed by DEBUG for the whole run. Hoisting the call above the per-user loop calls it once per batch instead of once per user. Each call costs about a hundred nanoseconds, so the saving is small. Blocked here, because the GraphQL batch needs GitHub.

decisions.label: c
decisions.why: The test if remaining at 658 always holds. Line 618 returns when remaining is empty, and the batch loop returns as soon as it empties remaining, so reaching 658 means remaining is non-empty. Removing the test drops one truthiness check per call and keeps every result. Blocked here, because the function needs GitHub.

what_it_does: inserts a member line into the Emeritus section of a README string, keeping member lines sorted by display name, or creates the section before the roles or licence heading

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: The regex match at 859, and again at 872, tests a fixed three-character prefix on every line of the section: a dash, asterisk or plus, then a space and an open bracket. line.startswith on a tuple of the three prefixes gives the same answer with no regex call and no match object. Lines come from split on newline, so the anchor sees no embedded newlines and behaves identically. Pure, so it is measurable here.

decisions.label: b
decisions.why: The index loop at 871-875 repeats the member test that the comprehension at 859 already made over the same lines, in order to find the first and last member indices. Recording those indices in one enumerate pass, and building member_lines from them, removes the second pass and gives the same new_lines. Pure, so it is measurable here.

what_it_does: finds an open follow-up issue with the cleanup title, paging through the repo's open issues, and updates its body, or creates the issue when none matches

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: Paging all open issues to find one title pulls more than the function reads. The cheaper lookup is the search API, which is eventually consistent: an issue created minutes earlier can be missing from search, and the function would then open a duplicate. That changes which issue is found, so the repair cannot keep the contract. Rejected on the behaviour check.

what_it_does: for each repo with inactive members, fetches the README, moves each member's line from its role sections to Emeritus, then opens or updates a PR, or a follow-up issue when the README is unchanged

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: For every user and each of its roles, the display name is found by locating the role section and parsing all of its members, at 1206-1210. The name comes from the user's own line, and an earlier iteration removes only other users' lines, since the removal regex matches the exact profile URL and ends at the closing parenthesis. So a lookup on the README before the loop returns the same name and list marker. One map built before the loop replaces the per-user scans. Blocked here, because fetch_readme needs GitHub.

what_it_does: collects team members and repos for each role, checks activity per repo, builds the inactive report, prints it, and optionally creates PRs

decisions.label: a
decisions.why: team_repos_map is assigned at 1356 and read nowhere in the file, so each team's set of repos is built and stored for nothing. Deleting the dict at 1304 and the assignment at 1356 removes one set per team and changes no output. Blocked here, because reaching line 1356 needs the GitHub API.
